title: Acyclicity of scalar-restricted K-injectives for diagonal direct image
statement: Fix a prime l and a scheme morphism f:X→S with DiagonalTraceLocalizations at X and S [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-models]. Let rX be any normalized Restriction from the actual varying E=ULift Q_l coefficient systems on X to strict constant Z_l systems on X [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-models]. Let Rf and Rt be any DiagonalRightDerived models, with their universal cochain units and K-injective computation [def-sfb-diagonal-limit-interface], of constant Z_l-module direct image along f and its strict-tower version respectively. For every K-injective varying-system complex I [def-pur-kinjective-complex], the unit Rt.η evaluated on the termwise rX.F image of I is an isomorphism. For every K-injective completed-module complex I, the unit Rf.η evaluated on the termwise diagonalCompletedRestriction l X image of I is an isomorphism. Neither scalar restriction is asserted to preserve K-injectives. No choice of coefficient/Chern data, ordinary comparison squares, or derived comparison isomorphisms occurs in the conclusion.

source.place: paragraph (1), scalar restrictions and direct-image comparisons before R lim

proof.text: Apply diagonalTrace_restriction_ringedModels to obtain the actual ring sheaves RX, RS, scalar map a, geometric map b, equivalences eX and eS and their two comparison isomorphisms. These are the explicit sequence-site and constant-section models, constructed independently of complexes. The proved helper is separated into its own module to keep each compile below the per-file limit.

For completed coefficients, the constantCommuteCompose unit equation constructs constantSectionsIso. This identifies diagonalCompletedRestriction with actual ring-sheaf scalar restriction followed by the constant-section equivalence. The constant direct-image structural map preserves constant sections by the sheafification adjunction, and the scalar-section direct-image square supplies the geometric comparison.

Use continuous_scalar_resolution and transport through the exact equivalences by quasiIso_map_of_models. For towers use the abstract ringed models and their comparison isomorphisms from the preceding helper. The geometric base-change functor is representably flat because it preserves finite limits; for product sites use the structured-arrow product equivalence. The resulting completed_resolution_quasiIso and tower_resolution_quasiIso concern the actual functors in the statement and assert no preservation of K-injectives by scalar restriction.

The Grothendieck abelian fixed-module sheaf category and its tower category admit K-injective resolutions. Resolve each restricted complex K by j:K→J. Naturality gives Q(Gj) followed by the derived unit on J equal to the derived unit on K followed by R(Qj). The resolution quasi-isomorphism lemmas make Q(Gj) invertible, computation makes the unit on J invertible, and Qj and its image under R are invertible. Cancel R(Qj) to prove invertibility of the unit on K for the supplied Rf and Rt. This is the private unit_isIso_of_resolution lemma and proves both conjuncts.

theorem diagonalTrace_restrictedPush_acyclic (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l X] [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) (rX : Restriction l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) X)
    (Rf : DiagonalRightDerived
      (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ_[l])) f))
    (Rt : DiagonalRightDerived (diagonalTraceSystemPush l f)) :
    (∀ I : CochainComplex (Systems X (Arings l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) X)) ℤ,
      I.IsKInjective →
        IsIso (Rt.η.app ((rX.F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I))) ∧
    (∀ I : CochainComplex (DiagonalCompleted l X) ℤ, I.IsKInjective →
      IsIso (Rf.η.app (((diagonalCompletedRestriction l X).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).obj I)))
